content.value_statement: Modern .NET backend work requires consistent choices for APIs, data access, caching, and tests. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical patterns for production C# services.
actual_capabilities: Explains clean architecture project structure for .NET APIs and MCP servers.
Provides dependency injection patterns for scoped, singleton, transient, and keyed services.
Guides async, cancellation, Result pattern, and configuration practices.
Compares EF Core and Dapper repository patterns with practical examples.
Covers caching, invalidation, unit tests, and integration test setup.
limitations: Does not execute, compile, or test generated .NET code.
Requires project-specific validation before production use.
Uses illustrative product and order domains that may need adaptation.
Does not replace security review for authentication or authorization design.

use_cases.title: Design a New API
use_cases.description: Plan folders, services, repositories, validation, caching, and tests for a new ASP.NET Core service.

use_cases.title: Review Data Access Choices
use_cases.description: Compare EF Core and Dapper patterns for query performance, maintainability, transactions, and repository boundaries.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Guidance
use_cases.description: Create shared .NET backend conventions for dependency injection, configuration, testing, and common anti-patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Web API Skeleton
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a .NET Web API for products. Include folders, service lifetimes, DTOs, validation, and test strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Review Async Service Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this C# service for async, cancellation, dependency injection, and Result pattern issues. Suggest concrete improvements with rationale.

prompt_templates.title: Choose EF Core or Dapper
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a data access layer for high-read product search. Compare EF Core and Dapper, then recommend repositories and caching boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Production Backend
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a production .NET backend for orders. Cover service boundaries, transactions, resilience, caching, tests, configuration, and operational risks.

output_examples.input: I need a repository design for product search with EF Core and Dapper.
output_examples.output: A concise comparison of repository boundaries, parameterized queries, pagination, cancellation, and when each data access tool fits best.

output_examples.input: Review this order service for async and validation issues.
output_examples.output: A review highlighting blocking calls, missing cancellation tokens, validation gaps, Result pattern usage, and targeted test cases.

output_examples.input: Plan caching for product lookups in an API.
output_examples.output: A cache design covering memory cache, Redis, expiration policy, invalidation, stale reads, and logging considerations.

best_practices: Validate generated patterns against your domain model, database provider, and deployment constraints.
Ask for tests and failure cases when using the skill for service or repository design.
Review security-sensitive flows separately, especially authentication, authorization, secrets, and external integrations.
anti_patterns: Do not copy sample domains directly into production without adapting names, validation, and policies.
Do not mix synchronous blocking calls into async request flows.
Do not choose Dapper or EF Core based only on preference; match the tool to query complexity.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design and review .NET backend services, APIs, repositories, caching layers, configuration, and tests.

faq.question: Does it support ASP.NET Core?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance targets modern ASP.NET Core APIs and related service architecture patterns.

faq.question: Can it generate complete applications?
faq.answer: It can guide structure and sample implementation, but you must integrate, compile, test, and secure the final application.

faq.question: When should I use EF Core instead of Dapper?
faq.answer: Use EF Core for rich domain models and change tracking. Use Dapper for focused, performance-sensitive queries.

faq.question: Does it include testing guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers xUnit, mocking, validation tests, integration tests, and WebApplicationFactory patterns.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: The reviewed content is documentation and templates only. Generated code still requires normal project review before use.
